current.text: The Lakers turned over more than half of their roster. LeBron James left for the Sixers, and Rui Hachimura appears to be gone too.
Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves are the remaining core.
The departures of LeBron James and Rui Hachimura open big usage for the players who remain, plus about 64 starting minutes at forward.
The front office wanted a younger, more athletic roster, with more players who can dribble, pass and shoot.
The team is aiming for a top five offense and a middle of the pack defense.
Two starting spots are open, mainly between Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia and Sandro Mamukelashvili. The current depth chart starts Mamukelashvili and Grimes.
Whoever of Grimes, LaRavia and Mamukelashvili comes off the bench will probably still play about 27 minutes.
Ziaire Williams might start for the Lakers.
The rotation choices under coach J.J. Redick are unclear.
Walker Kessler is the starting center. The backup centers are weak, with Kevon Looney behind him.
The defense depends heavily on Kessler. If he is out, the team would have to rely on Looney or Mamukelashvili.
Mamukelashvili should get the backup center minutes over Looney.
Lloyd thinks the roster lacks defenders around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves.
Andy predicts 50 wins and a top six finish in the West. He thinks the lack of continuity probably keeps them out of the conference finals.
Luka Doncic's health makes the Lakers more vulnerable than the top five West teams.
The schedule is about average for rest risk and for our fantasy playoffs. Back-to-backs and playoff week games both rank in the middle of the league.

note: With LeBron James and Rui Hachimura gone, Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves get more usage, and the open forward minutes help whoever wins the starting jobs. Walker Kessler carries the defense with weak backup centers behind him, and Sandro Mamukelashvili should pick up the backup center minutes. Early on, watch who starts among Grimes, LaRavia, Mamukelashvili and Ziaire Williams, and whether Luka stays healthy.
